title: Hal Higdon Intermediate 5K Training Program (8 weeks)
population: Experienced runners who have raced a 5K, running 3-4 days a week for a year or two at 15-20 miles per week
findings: Sunday long run by week: 5, 5, 6, 5K test, 6, 7, 7 miles, then the 5K race in week 8; the page header lists a longest workout of 7 miles.
Typical week is 5 run days with Monday and Friday as rest; other runs are 3-5 mi easy or fast runs and one weekly interval or tempo session (30-40 min tempo, 400 m repeats).

The page states the audience as 'running 3-4 days a week for the last year or two and averaging 15-20 miles weekly'; a 5-7 mile long run is therefore about 25-47% of the assumed weekly miles (own arithmetic: 5/20 to 7/15), with the peak 7 miles at roughly 35-47%.
limitations: Read through a page-fetch summariser; the weekly-share arithmetic is the auditor's own from the stated 15-20 mpw audience. Convention, not evidence. Year is the access date.
implications: Medium-volume 5K runners (15-20 miles, roughly 2.5-3.5 h/week) are given a long run of up to 7 miles (about 60-75 min at easy pace, estimate), consistent with a 60-75 min medium-tier cap.
The implied peak share is about 35-47% of weekly distance, above Daniels' 30% guidance, so a share cap near 35-40% would be the upper end of coach practice.

verification.notes: Re-fetched halhigdon.com intermediate 5K page 2026-10-22: Sunday entries 5/5/6/test/6/7/7/race, 'Longest workout 7 miles' and both audience quotes confirmed. Published convention, not evidence.
